## Health

### check

`health.check`

Runs a full health check testing as many services and systems as possible. These health checks can be expensive operations such as writing files to storage etc.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.health.check({});
```

**Input:** _empty object_


**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `passing` | `boolean \| null` | No | False if any of the critical service health checks are failing, true otherwise. |
| `checks` | `Record<string, string> \| null` | No | An object keyed by the name of the health check and the value being the result. |
| `celery_queue_size` | `number \| null` | No | The number of enqueued celery tasks. |
| `celery_export_queue_size` | `number \| null` | No | The number of enqueued celery export worker tasks. |



---

### checkCeleryQueueSize

`health.checkCeleryQueueSize`

Health check endpoint to check if the celery, export and/or chat_run queue has exceeded the maximum healthy size. Responds with 200 if there there are less than 10 in all queues provided. Otherwise responds with a 503.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.health.checkCeleryQueueSize({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `queue` | `string` | No | The name of the queues to check. Can be provided multiple times. Accepts `celery`, `export` or `chat_run`. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |



---

### testEmail

`health.testEmail`

Sends a test email to the provided email address. Useful for testing Baserow's email configuration as errors are clearly returned.

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.health.testEmail({ target_email: 'ada@example.com' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `target_email` | `string` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `succeeded` | `boolean \| null` | No | Whether or not the test email was sent successfully. |
| `error_stack` | `string \| null \| null` | No | The full stack trace and error message if the test email failed. |
| `error_type` | `string \| null \| null` | No | The type of error that occurred if the test email failed. |
| `error` | `string \| null \| null` | No | A short message describing the error that occured if the test email failed |



---

## Identities

### create

`identities.create`

Creates a new identity in a workspace. (POST /api/identities/workspace/&#123;workspace_id&#125;/)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.identities.create({ workspace_id: 101, name: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `workspace_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The workspace whose identities are being managed. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `role_uid` | `string` | No | — |

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.integrations.completeMcpServerOauth({ state: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `state` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `code` | `string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `application_id` | `number \| null` | No | — |

### create

`integrations.create`

Creates a new integration. (POST /api/application/&#123;application_id&#125;/integrations/)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.integrations.create({ application_id: 1, name: 'example', type: 'local_baserow' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `application_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Creates an integration for the application related to the provided value. |
| `before_id` | `number` | No | If provided, creates the integration before the integration with the given id. |
| `type` | `local_baserow \| smtp \| ai \| slack_bot \| mcp_server` | Yes | The type of the integration. * `local_baserow` - local_baserow * `smtp` - smtp * `ai` - ai * `slack_bot` - slack_bot * `mcp_server` - mcp_server |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `authorized_subject_id` | `number \| null` | No | The ID of the subject whose permissions authenticate the integration. |
| `authorized_subject_type` | `auth.User \| never \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `host` | `string` | No | The SMTP server hostname or IP address. |
| `port` | `number` | No | The SMTP server port. |
| `use_tls` | `boolean` | No | Whether to upgrade the connection with STARTTLS. |
| `use_ssl` | `boolean` | No | Whether to connect with implicit SSL/TLS, usually on port 465. |
| `username` | `string \| null` | No | The SMTP username for authentication. |
| `password` | `string \| null` | No | The SMTP password. Write-only: it is never returned, see `has_password`. Omit it to keep the stored password; send an empty string or null to clear it. |
| `ai_settings` | `any` | No | Per-provider AI settings overrides. On update, omit a provider's `api_key` to keep the stored one; it must be supplied again when any other connection setting of that provider changes. |
| `token` | `string` | No | The Bot User OAuth Token. Write-only: it is never returned, see `has_token`. Omit it on an update to keep the stored token. |
| `url` | `string` | No | The Streamable HTTP endpoint of the MCP server. |
| `auth_type` | `none \| header \| oauth` | No | * `none` - None * `header` - Header * `oauth` - Oauth |
| `auth_header_name` | `string` | No | The header that carries the credential, e.g. Authorization. |
| `auth_header_value` | `string` | No | The credential sent in the auth header. Write-only: it is never returned, see `has_auth_header_value`. Omit it on an update to keep the stored value. |
| `oauth_client_id` | `string` | No | The OAuth client id, entered by an editor or registered by Baserow. |
| `oauth_client_secret` | `string` | No | The OAuth client secret. |



**Output:** `object`

| `use_ssl` | `boolean` | No | Whether to connect with implicit SSL/TLS, usually on port 465. |
| `username` | `string \| null` | No | The SMTP username for authentication. |
| `password` | `string \| null` | No | The SMTP password. Write-only: it is never returned, see `has_password`. Omit it to keep the stored password; send an empty string or null to clear it. |
| `ai_settings` | `any` | No | Per-provider AI settings overrides. On update, omit a provider's `api_key` to keep the stored one; it must be supplied again when any other connection setting of that provider changes. |
| `token` | `string` | No | The Bot User OAuth Token. Write-only: it is never returned, see `has_token`. Omit it on an update to keep the stored token. |
| `url` | `string` | No | The Streamable HTTP endpoint of the MCP server. |
| `auth_type` | `none \| header \| oauth` | No | * `none` - None * `header` - Header * `oauth` - Oauth |
| `auth_header_name` | `string` | No | The header that carries the credential, e.g. Authorization. |
| `auth_header_value` | `string` | No | The credential sent in the auth header. Write-only: it is never returned, see `has_auth_header_value`. Omit it on an update to keep the stored value. |
| `oauth_client_id` | `string` | No | The OAuth client id, entered by an editor or registered by Baserow. |
| `oauth_client_secret` | `string` | No | The OAuth client secret. |



**Output:** `object`

### updateMcpServerTools

`integrations.updateMcpServerTools`

Turns the given tools on or off and sets whether they change data. Saving a tool marks its current definition as reviewed.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.integrations.updateMcpServerTools({ integration_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `integration_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The id of the MCP server integration. |
| `tools` | `object[]` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="tools full type">

```ts
{
  name: string,
  enabled?: boolean,
  ask_first?: boolean,
  definition_hash?: string
}[]
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `application_id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `type` | `any \| null` | No | The type of the integration. |
| `name` | `any \| null` | No | — |
| `order` | `string \| null` | No | Lowest first. |

## Jobs

### cancel

`jobs.cancel`

Cancels a job. Note: you can cancel only a scheduled or a job that is already running. The user requesting must be the owner of the job to cancel.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.jobs.cancel({ job_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `job_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The job id to cancel. |



**Output:** `object`

### create

`jobs.create`

Creates a new job. This job runs asynchronously in the background and execute the task specific to the provided typeparameters. The get_job can be used to get the current state of the job.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.jobs.create({ type: 'duplicate_application' });
```

---

### get

`jobs.get`

Returns the information related to the provided job id. This endpoint can for example be polled to get the state and progress of the job in real time.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.jobs.get({ job_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `job_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The job id to lookup information about. |



**Output:** `object`

---

### list

`jobs.list`

List all existing jobs. Jobs are task executed asynchronously in the background. You can use the get_job endpoint to read the current progress of the job. The available query parameters depend on the job type selected via the type parameter. Each job type may support additional type-specific….

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.jobs.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `generate_ai_values_field_id` | `number \| string` | No | **[Only for type='generate_ai_values']** Filter by the AI field ID. |
| `job_ids` | `string` | No | — |
| `limit` | `number` | No | — |
| `offset` | `number` | No | — |
| `states` | `string` | No | — |
| `sync_data_sync_table_data_sync_id` | `number \| string` | No | **[Only for type='sync_data_sync_table']** Filter by the data sync ID. |
| `type` | `duplicate_application \| install_template \| create_snapshot \| restore_snapshot \| export_applications \| import_applications \| create_user_template \| download_user_template \| airtable \| duplicate_table \| duplicate_field \| sync_data_sync_table \| button_field_dispatch \| duplicate_page \| publish_domain \| duplicate_automation_workflow \| publish_automation_workflow \| generate_ai_values \| audit_log_export \| data_scan_result_export \| file_import` | No | The type of job to filter for. Determines which additional filter fields are available. * `duplicate_application` - duplicate_application * `install_template` - install_template * `create_snapshot` - create_snapshot * `restore_snapshot` - restore_snapshot * `export_applications` - export_applications * `import_applications` - import_applications * `create_user_template` - create_user_template * `download_user_template` - download_user_template * `airtable` - airtable * `duplicate_table` - duplicate_table * `duplicate_field` - duplicate_field * `sync_data_sync_table` - sync_data_sync_table * `button_field_dispatch` - button_field_dispatch * `duplicate_page` - duplicate_page * `publish_domain` - publish_domain * `duplicate_automation_workflow` - duplicate_automation_workflow * `publish_automation_workflow` - publish_automation_workflow * `generate_ai_values` - generate_ai_values * `audit_log_export` - audit_log_export * `data_scan_result_export` - data_scan_result_export * `file_import` - file_import |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `jobs` | `object[] \| null` | No | — |
| `count` | `number \| null \| null` | No | The number of matching jobs, or null when polling explicit job IDs. |

## Last Viewed

### listItems

`lastViewed.listItems`

Lists the views, application pages, dashboards, automation workflows and agents the authenticated user opened most recently, newest first. Only items the user can still access are returned.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.lastViewed.listItems({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `cursor` | `string` | No | The `next_cursor` of the previous page, omitted for the first page. The next page continues after the last item of the previous one, even when items were viewed in between. |
| `limit` | `number` | No | Maximum number of items to return, 20 by default and 100 at most. |
| `types` | `string` | No | Comma separated item types, optionally limited to a sub type with `type:sub_type`, like `database_view:grid,builder_page`. Defaults to every type. |
| `workspace_ids` | `string` | No | Comma separated ids of the workspaces to list items of. Defaults to every workspace the user is a member of. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | — |
| `next_cursor` | `string \| null \| null` | No | Pass as `cursor` to get the next page, `null` when no more items follow. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="results full type">

```ts
{
  type?: string | null,
  sub_type?: string | null | null,
  last_viewed?: string | null,
  application?: {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null,
    type?: any | null
  } | null,
  workspace?: {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null
  } | null,
  item?: {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null,
    table?: {
      id?: number | null,
      name?: string | null
    } | null
  } | {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null
  } | {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null
  } | {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null
  } | {
    id?: number | null,
    name?: string | null
  } | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Mcp Endpoints

### create

`mcpEndpoints.create`

Creates a new MCP endpoint for a given workspace. The endpoint can be used for an MCP integration.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.mcpEndpoints.create({ name: 'example', workspace_id: 101 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | The human readable name of the MCP endpoint for the user. |
| `workspace_id` | `number` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | The human readable name of the MCP endpoint for the user. |
| `key` | `any \| null \| null` | No | The unique endpoint key that can be used to authorize for the MCP service. Null for OAuth grants, which only accept their access tokens. |
| `workspace_id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `workspace_name` | `any \| null` | No | — |
| `allowed_tools` | `string[] \| null` | No | — |
| `created` | `string \| null` | No | — |



---

```ts

```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `endpoint_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### list

`mcpEndpoints.list`

Lists all the MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoints of a user. These canbe used to directly integrate with an LLM like Claude, and let the LLM perform actions directly in Baserow. Treat your MCP URL like a password,as it has the ability to modify data in Baserow.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.mcpEndpoints.list({});
```

**Input:** _empty object_


**Output:** `object[]`

```ts
  name?: string | null,
  key?: any | null | null,
  workspace_id?: number | null,
  workspace_name?: any | null,
  allowed_tools?: string[] | null,
  created?: string | null
}[]
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Notifications

`notifications.clear`

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.notifications.clear({ workspace_id: 101 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `workspace_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The workspace the notifications are in. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |



---

### list

`notifications.list`

Lists the notifications for the given workspace and the current user. The response is paginated and the limit and offset parameters can be controlled using the query parameters.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.notifications.list({ workspace_id: 101 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `limit` | `number` | No | Defines how many notifications should be returned. |
| `offset` | `number` | No | Defines the offset of the notifications that should be returned. |
| `workspace_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The workspace id that the notifications belong to. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `count` | `number \| null` | No | The total amount of results. |
| `next` | `string \| null \| null` | No | URL to the next page. |
| `previous` | `string \| null \| null` | No | URL to the previous page. |
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="results full type">

```ts
{
  id?: number | null,
  type?: string | null,
  sender?: {
    id?: number | null,
    username?: any | null | null,
    first_name?: string | null,
    user_type?: any | null
  } | null,
  workspace?: any | null,
  created_on?: string | null,
  read?: boolean | null,
  data?: any | null
}[] | null
```

### markAsRead

`notifications.markAsRead`

Marks a notification as read. (PATCH /api/notifications/&#123;workspace_id&#125;/&#123;notification_id&#125;/)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.notifications.markAsRead({ notification_id: 1, workspace_id: 101 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `notification_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The notification id to update. |
| `workspace_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The workspace the notification is in. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | The id of the notification. |
| `type` | `string \| null` | No | The type of notification |
| `sender` | `object \| null` | No | The user that sent the notification. |
| `workspace` | `any \| null` | No | The workspace that the notification is in (if any). |
| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | The date and time that the notification was created. |
| `read` | `boolean \| null` | No | If True, then the notification has been read by the user. |
| `data` | `any \| null` | No | The data associated with the notification. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="sender full type">

```ts
{
```

## Role Assignments

### assign

`roleAssignments.assign`

You can assign a role to a subject into the given workspace for the given scope with this endpoint. If you want to remove the role you can omit the role property.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.roleAssignments.assign({
	workspace_id: 101,
	role: 'example',
	scope_id: 1,
	scope_type: 'core',
	subject_id: 1,
	subject_type: 'auth.User',
});
```

### createScopedInvitation

`roleAssignments.createScopedInvitation`

Invites an email address to one scope of the workspace. The person joins the workspace without a workspace role and gets the given role on the scope once they accept. If a pending invitation already exists for the address, the scope is added to it. The invitation email is sent out immediately.

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.roleAssignments.createScopedInvitation({
	workspace_id: 101,
	email: 'ada@example.com',
	role: 'example',
	scope_id: 1,
	scope_type: 'core',
});
```

### deleteScopedInvitation

`roleAssignments.deleteScopedInvitation`

Revokes the role a pending invitation grants on its scope. The invitation itself and its other scopes are kept.

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.roleAssignments.deleteScopedInvitation({ scoped_invitation_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `scoped_invitation_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The scoped invitation to revoke. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |



---

### deleteScopedInvitationLink

`roleAssignments.deleteScopedInvitationLink`

Deletes a permanent invitation link to a scope, after which it can't be used anymore. People who joined through it keep their role.

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.roleAssignments.deleteScopedInvitationLink({ invitation_link_id: 1 });
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `invitation_link_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The invitation link to delete. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### batchCreate

`rows.batchCreate`

Creates new rows in the table if the user has access to the related table's workspace. The accepted body fields are depending on the fields that the table has. For a complete overview of fields use the list_database_table_fields to list them all. None of the fields are required, if they are not…. Takes a database token or a signed-in user.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.rows.batchCreate({
	table_id: 1001,
	items: [{}],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `before` | `number` | No | If provided then the newly created rows will be positioned before the row with the provided id. |
| `include_metadata` | `boolean` | No | if provided, this will include `metadata` key containing operation metadata information in the response. Metadata will include a list of field ids, that were changed during the operation. The list will be stored in `update_field_ids` key in `metadata` object. Also, metadata object will include `cascade_update` key with a list of rows updated in cascade, and a list of field ids that were updated in cascade update. |
| `send_webhook_events` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that triggers webhooks after the operation, if set to `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or left empty. Defaults to `true` |
| `table_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Creates the rows in the table. |
| `user_field_names` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that, if provided with one of the following values: `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or an empty value, will cause this endpoint to expect and return the user-specified field names instead of the internal Baserow field names (e.g., field_123). |
| `view` | `number` | No | Provide if the rows are created in a view. This can result in different permission checking and default values. |
| `items` | `Record<string, any>[]` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `Record<string, any>[] \| null` | No | — |

### getAdjacent

`rows.getAdjacent`

Fetches the adjacent row to a given row_id in the table with the given table_id. If the previous flag is set it will return the previous row, otherwise it will return the next row. You can specifya view_id and it will apply the filters and sorts of the provided view.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.rows.getAdjacent({ row_id: 1, table_id: 1001 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `previous` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter which if provided returns theprevious row to the specified row_id. If it's not setit will return the next row. |
| `row_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Returns the row adjacent the provided value. |
| `search` | `string` | No | If provided, the adjacent row will be one that matchesthe search query. |
| `search_mode` | `string` | No | If provided, allows API consumers to determine what kind of search experience they wish to have. If the default `SearchMode.FT_WITH_COUNT` is used, then Postgres full-text search is used. If `SearchMode.COMPAT` is provided then the search term will be exactly searched for including whitespace on each cell. This is the Baserow legacy search behaviour. |
| `table_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Returns the row of the table related to the provided value. |
| `user_field_names` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that, if provided with one of the following values: `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or an empty value, will cause the returned JSON to use the user-specified field names instead of the internal Baserow field names (e.g., field_123). |
| `view_id` | `number \| string` | No | Applies the filters and sorts of the provided view. |



**Output:** `object`

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Output full type">

```ts
{
  id?: number | null,
  order?: string | null,
  metadata?: {
    row_comment_count?: number | null,
    row_comments_notification_mode?: string | null
  } | null
} | {
  success: true
}
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### list

`rows.list`

Lists all the rows of the table related to the provided parameter if the user has access to the related database's workspace. The response is paginated by a page/size style. It is also possible to provide an optional search query, only rows where the data matches the search query are going to be…. Takes a database token or a signed-in user. Set user_field_names to true to read and write fields by name instead of field_&lt;id&gt;.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.rows.list({ table_id: 1001, user_field_names: true, size: 20 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `exclude` | `string` | No | All the fields are included in the response by default. You can select a subset of fields by providing the exclude query parameter. If you for example provide the following GET parameter `exclude=field_1,field_2` then the fields with id `1` and id `2` are going to be excluded from the selection and response. If the `user_field_names` parameter is provided then instead exclude should be a comma separated list of the actual field names. For field names with commas you should surround the name with quotes like so: `exclude=My Field,"Field With , "`. A backslash can be used to escape field names which contain double quotes like so: `exclude=My Field,Field with \\"`. |
| `filter__{field}__{filter}` | `string` | No | The rows can optionally be filtered by the same view filters available for the views. Multiple filters can be provided if they follow the same format. The field and filter variable indicate how to filter and the value indicates where to filter on. For example if you provide the following GET parameter `filter__field_1__equal=test` then only rows where the value of field_1 is equal to test are going to be returned. ### listNames

`rows.listNames`

Returns the names of the given row of the given tables. The nameof a row is the primary field value for this row. The result can be usedfor example, when you want to display the name of a linked row from another table. Takes a database token or a signed-in user.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.rows.listNames({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `table__{id}` | `string` | No | A list of comma separated row ids to query from the table with id &#123;id&#125;. For example, if you want the name of row `42` and `43` from table `28` this parameter will be `table__28=42,43`. You can specify multiple rows for different tables but every tables must be in the same database. You need at least read permission on all specified tables. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `{table_id}*` | `object \| null` | No | An object containing the row names of table `table_id`. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="{table_id}* full type">

```ts
{
  {
    row_id
  }*?: string | null
} | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### move

`rows.move`

Moves the row related to given row_id parameter to another position. It is only possible to move the row before another existing row or to the end. If the before_id is provided then the row related to the row_id parameter is moved before that row. If the before_id parameter is not provided, then…. Takes a database token or a signed-in user.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.rows.move({ row_id: 1, table_id: 1001 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `before_id` | `number \| string` | No | Moves the row related to the given `row_id` before the row related to the provided value. If not provided, then the row will be moved to the end. |
| `row_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Moves the row related to the value. |
| `send_webhook_events` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that triggers webhooks after the operation, if set to `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or left empty. Defaults to `true` |
| `table_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Moves the row in the table related to the value. |
| `user_field_names` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that, if provided with one of the following values: `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or an empty value, will cause the returned JSON to use the user-specified field names instead of the internal Baserow field names (e.g., field_123). |
| `view` | `number` | No | Provide if the row is moved in a view. This can result in different permission checking. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | The unique identifier of the row in the table. |
| `order` | `string \| null` | No | Indicates the position of the row, lowest first and highest last. |
| `metadata` | `object \| null` | No | Additional metadata for the row, if `include=metadata' is provided as query parameter. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="metadata full type">

```ts
{
  row_comment_count?: number | null,
  row_comments_notification_mode?: string | null
} | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### update

`rows.update`

Updates an existing row in the table if the user has access to the related table's workspace. The accepted body fields are depending on the fields that the table has. For a complete overview of fields use the list_database_table_fields endpoint to list them all. None of the fields are required,…. Takes a database token or a signed-in user. Pass the changed field values next to table_id and row_id, keyed field_&lt;id&gt; or (with user_field_names: true) by name.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.rows.update({ row_id: 1, table_id: 1001 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `row_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Updates the row related to the value. |
| `send_webhook_events` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that triggers webhooks after the operation, if set to `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or left empty. Defaults to `true` |
| `table_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Updates the row in the table related to the value. |
| `user_field_names` | `boolean` | No | A flag query parameter that, if provided with one of the following values: `y`, `yes`, `true`, `t`, `on`, `1`, or an empty value, will cause this endpoint to expect and return the user-specified field names instead of the internal Baserow field names (e.g., field_123). |
| `view` | `number` | No | Provide if the row is updated in a view. This can result in different permission checking and default values. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | The unique identifier of the row in the table. |
| `order` | `string \| null` | No | Indicates the position of the row, lowest first and highest last. |
| `metadata` | `object \| null` | No | Additional metadata for the row, if `include=metadata' is provided as query parameter. |

```ts
{
  row_comment_count?: number | null,

} | null
```

## Secure Files

### download

`secureFiles.download`

Downloads a file using the backend and the secure file serve feature. The signed data is extracted from the URL and used to verify if the user has access to the file. If the permissions check passes and the file exists, the file is served to the user. This is a enterprise feature. Public: no sign-in.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.secureFiles.download({ signed_data: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `signed_data` | `string` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

## Settings

### get

`settings.get`

Responds with all the admin configured settings. Public: no sign-in.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.settings.get({});
```

**Input:** _empty object_


**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `allow_new_signups` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether new users can create a new account when signing up. |
| `allow_signups_via_workspace_invitations` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether invited users can create an account when signing up, even if allow_new_signups is disabled. |
| `allow_reset_password` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether users can request a password reset link. |
| `allow_global_workspace_creation` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether all users can create workspaces, or just staff. |
| `account_deletion_grace_delay` | `number \| null` | No | Number of days after the last login for an account pending deletion to be deleted |
| `show_admin_signup_page` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates that there are no admin users in the database yet, so in the frontend the signup form will be shown instead of the login page. |
| `track_workspace_usage` | `boolean \| null` | No | Runs a job once per day which calculates per workspace row counts and file storage usage, displayed on the admin workspace page. |
| `show_baserow_help_request` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether the `We need your help!` message will be shown on the dashboard |
| `co_branding_logo` | `object \| null` | No | Co-branding logo that's placed next to the Baserow logo (176x29). |
| `email_verification` | `string \| any \| null \| null \| null` | No | Controls whether user email addresses have to be verified. * `no_verification` - no_verification * `recommended` - recommended * `enforced` - enforced |
| `verify_import_signature` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether the signature of imported files should be verified. |
| `allow_reporting_abuse` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether anonymous visitors can report publicly shared resources, like views and forms, for abuse. |
| `user_templates_require_approval` | `boolean \| null` | No | Whether a user template made public, and every edit of a listed one, is listed only once an instance admin approves it. Switching it off approves the templates in review that an admin could approve, except the ones rejected since their last approval. Can only be changed with the user templates feature enabled. |
| `inbound_email_enabled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Whether this instance is configured to receive inbound email for the automation email trigger. Derived from the instance's environment and read-only. |
| `email_delivery_enabled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Whether this instance is configured to deliver emails, for example invitations and email verifications. Derived from the instance's environment and read-only. |

## Snapshots

### create

`snapshots.create`

Creates a new application snapshot. Snapshots represent a state of an application at a specific point in time and can be restored later, making it easy to create backups of entire applications.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.snapshots.create({ application_id: 1, name: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `application_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Application ID for which to list snapshots. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `type` | `any \| null` | No | The type of the job. |
| `progress_percentage` | `number \| null` | No | A percentage indicating how far along the job is. 100 means that it's finished. |
| `state` | `string \| null` | No | Indicates the state of the import job. |
| `human_readable_error` | `string \| null` | No | A human readable error message indicating what went wrong. |
| `error_code` | `string \| null` | No | A machine readable error code indicating why the job failed. |
| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `updated_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |



---

### delete

`snapshots.delete`

Deletes a snapshot. Deleting a snapshot doesn't affect the application that the snapshot is made from and doesn't affect any applications that were created by restoring it. Snapshot deletion is permanent and can't be undone.

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.snapshots.delete({ snapshot_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `snapshot_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Id of the snapshot to delete. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |



---

### list

`snapshots.list`

Lists snapshots that were created for a given application.

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.snapshots.list({ application_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `application_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Application ID for which to list snapshots. |



**Output:** `object[]`

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Output full type">

```ts
{
  id?: number | null,
  name?: string | null,
  snapshot_from_application?: number | null,
  created_at?: string | null,
  created_by?: {
    username?: string | null
  } | null
}[]
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


---

`snapshots.restore`

Restores a snapshot. When an application snapshot is restored, a new application will be created in the same workspace that the original application was placed in with the name of the snapshot and data that were in the original application at the time the snapshot was taken. The original….

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts

```

|------|------|----------|-------------|

**Output**

|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `type` | `any \| null` | No | The type of the job. |
| `progress_percentage` | `number \| null` | No | A percentage indicating how far along the job is. 100 means that it's finished. |

## Tables

### create

`tables.create`

Creates synchronously a new table for the database related to the provided database_id parameter if the authorized user has access to the database's workspace. As an alternative you can use the create_async_database_table for better performances and importing bigger files.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.tables.create({ database_id: 1, name: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `database_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Creates a table for the database related to the provided value. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `data` | `any[][]` | No | A list of rows that needs to be created as initial table data. Each row is a list of values that are going to be added in the new table in the same order as provided. Ex: ```json [ ["row1_field1_value", "row1_field2_value"], ["row2_field1_value", "row2_field2_value"], ] ``` for creating a two rows table with two fields. If not provided, some example data is going to be created. |
| `first_row_header` | `boolean` | No | Indicates if the first provided row is the header. If true the field names are going to be the values of the first row. Otherwise they will be called "Field N" |
| `importer_type` | `string` | No | The frontend importer identifier used to parse the file. |
| `original_file_name` | `string` | No | The original name of the uploaded file. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `order` | `number \| null` | No | Lowest first. |
| `database_id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `data_sync` | `object \| null` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="data_sync full type">

```ts
{
  id?: number | null,
  type?: any | null,
  table_id?: number | null,
  database_id?: any | null,
  synced_properties?: {
    field_id?: number | null,
    key?: string | null,
    unique_primary?: boolean | null
  }[] | null,
  last_sync?: string | null | null,
  last_error?: string | null | null,
  auto_add_new_properties?: boolean | null,
  delete_unmatched_rows?: boolean | null,
  two_way_sync?: boolean | null
} | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

If not provided, some example data is going to be created. |

### dataSync.create

`tables.dataSync.create`

Creates a new data sync table with the given data sync type. This will technically create a table, but it's synchronized with the provided data sync information. This means that some fields related to it will automatically be created and will be read-only.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.tables.dataSync.create({
	database_id: 1,
	synced_properties: ['example'],
	table_name: 'example',
	type: 'ical_calendar',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `database_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Creates a data sync table for the database related to theprovided value. |
| `synced_properties` | `string[]` | Yes | — |
| `type` | `ical_calendar \| local_baserow_table \| jira_issues \| github_issues \| gitlab_issues \| hubspot_contacts \| postgresql` | Yes | The type of the data sync table that must be created. * `ical_calendar` - ical_calendar * `local_baserow_table` - local_baserow_table * `jira_issues` - jira_issues * `github_issues` - github_issues * `gitlab_issues` - gitlab_issues * `hubspot_contacts` - hubspot_contacts * `postgresql` - postgresql |
| `table_name` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `auto_add_new_properties` | `boolean` | No | If enabled and new properties are detected on sync, then they're automatically added. Note that this means all properties will always be added. |
| `delete_unmatched_rows` | `boolean` | No | If enabled, rows that are no longer present in the source are deleted from the synced table on every sync. If disabled, those rows are kept and reused if the matching source row reappears. |
| `two_way_sync` | `boolean` | No | If enabled, then it's possible to make changes to the synced table. They will automatically be synced with the source data. Note that this is only possible if the data sync type has a two-way sync strategy. |
| `ical_url` | `string` | No | — |
| `source_table_id` | `number` | No | The ID of the source table that must be synced. |
| `source_table_view_id` | `number \| null` | No | If provided, then only the visible fields and rows matching the filters will be synced. |
| `jira_url` | `string` | No | The base URL of your Jira instance (e.g., https://your-domain.atlassian.net). |
| `jira_project_key` | `string` | No | The project key of the Jira project (e.g., PROJ). |
| `jira_authentication` | `API_TOKEN \| PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` | No | * `API_TOKEN` - API_TOKEN * `PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` - PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN |
| `jira_username` | `string` | No | The username of the Jira account used to authenticate. Is only used if the `jira_authentication` is equal `API_TOKEN` |
| `github_issues_owner` | `string` | No | The owner of the repository on GitHub. |
| `github_issues_repo` | `string` | No | The name of the repository on GitHub. |
| `gitlab_url` | `string` | No | The base URL to your GitLab instance (e.g. https://gitlab.com) |
| `gitlab_project_id` | `string` | No | The ID of the GitLab project where to sync the issues with. |
| `postgresql_host` | `string` | No | — |
| `postgresql_username` | `string` | No | — |
| `postgresql_port` | `number` | No | — |
| `postgresql_database` | `string` | No | — |
| `postgresql_schema` | `string` | No | — |
| `postgresql_table` | `string` | No | — |
| `postgresql_sslmode` | `disable \| allow \| prefer \| require \| verify-ca \| verify-full` | No | * `disable` - disable * `allow` - allow * `prefer` - prefer * `require` - require * `verify-ca` - verify-ca * `verify-full` - verify-full |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `order` | `number \| null` | No | Lowest first. |
| `database_id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `data_sync` | `object \| null` | No | — |

```ts
  id?: number | null,
  type?: any | null,
  table_id?: number | null,
  database_id?: any | null,
  synced_properties?: {
    field_id?: number | null,
    key?: string | null,
    unique_primary?: boolean | null
  }[] | null,
  last_sync?: string | null | null,
  last_error?: string | null | null,

} | null
```

### dataSync.update

`tables.dataSync.update`

Updates the properties of the provided data sync, if the user has the right permissions. Note that if the synced_properties is not provided, the available properties change, then the unavailable ones will automatically be removed.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts

```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `data_sync_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Updates the data sync related to the provided value. |
| `synced_properties` | `string[]` | No | — |
| `auto_add_new_properties` | `boolean` | No | If enabled and new properties are detected on sync, then they're automatically added. Note that this means all properties will always be added. |
| `delete_unmatched_rows` | `boolean` | No | If enabled, rows that are no longer present in the source are deleted from the synced table on every sync. If disabled, those rows are kept and reused if the matching source row reappears. |
| `two_way_sync` | `boolean` | No | If enabled, then it's possible to make changes to the synced table. They will automatically be synced with the source data. Note that this is only possible if the data sync type has a two-way sync strategy. |

| `source_table_id` | `number` | No | The ID of the source table that must be synced. |


**Input**

| `export_charset` | `utf-8 \| iso-8859-6 \| windows-1256 \| iso-8859-4 \| windows-1257 \| iso-8859-14 \| iso-8859-2 \| windows-1250 \| gbk \| gb18030 \| big5 \| koi8-r \| koi8-u \| iso-8859-5 \| windows-1251 \| x-mac-cyrillic \| iso-8859-7 \| windows-1253 \| iso-8859-8 \| windows-1255 \| euc-jp \| iso-2022-jp \| shift-jis \| euc-kr \| macintosh \| iso-8859-10 \| iso-8859-16 \| windows-874 \| windows-1254 \| windows-1258 \| iso-8859-1 \| windows-1252 \| iso-8859-3` | No | The character set to use when creating the export file. * `utf-8` - utf-8 * `iso-8859-6` - iso-8859-6 * `windows-1256` - windows-1256 * `iso-8859-4` - iso-8859-4 * `windows-1257` - windows-1257 * `iso-8859-14` - iso-8859-14 * `iso-8859-2` - iso-8859-2 * `windows-1250` - windows-1250 * `gbk` - gbk * `gb18030` - gb18030 * `big5` - big5 * `koi8-r` - koi8-r * `koi8-u` - koi8-u * `iso-8859-5` - iso-8859-5 * `windows-1251` - windows-1251 * `x-mac-cyrillic` - mac-cyrillic * `iso-8859-7` - iso-8859-7 * `windows-1253` - windows-1253 * `iso-8859-8` - iso-8859-8 * `windows-1255` - windows-1255 * `euc-jp` - euc-jp * `iso-2022-jp` - iso-2022-jp * `shift-jis` - shift-jis * `euc-kr` - euc-kr * `macintosh` - macintosh * `iso-8859-10` - iso-8859-10 * `iso-8859-16` - iso-8859-16 * `windows-874` - cp874 * `windows-1254` - windows-1254 * `windows-1258` - windows-1258 * `iso-8859-1` - iso-8859-1 * `windows-1252` - windows-1252 * `iso-8859-3` - iso-8859-3 |
| `filters` | `object \| null` | No | A JSON serialized string containing the filter tree to apply to this view. The filter tree is a nested structure containing the filters that need to be applied. An example of a valid filter tree is the following:`{"filter_type": "AND", "filters": [{"field": 1, "type": "equal", "value": "test"}]}`. The `field` value must be the ID of the field to filter on, or the name of the field if `user_field_names` is true. The following filters are available: equal, not_equal, filename_contains, files_lower_than, has_file_type, contains, contains_not, contains_word, doesnt_contain_word, starts_with, length_is_lower_than, higher_than, higher_than_or_equal, lower_than, lower_than_or_equal, is_even_and_whole, date_equal, date_before, date_before_or_equal, date_after_days_ago, date_after, date_after_or_equal, date_not_equal, date_equals_today, date_before_today, date_after_today, date_within_days, date_within_weeks, date_within_months, date_equals_days_ago, date_equals_months_ago, date_equals_years_ago, date_equals_week, date_equals_month, date_equals_day_of_month, date_equals_year, date_is, date_is_not, date_is_before, date_is_on_or_before, date_is_after, date_is_on_or_after, date_is_within, single_select_equal, single_select_not_equal, single_select_is_any_of, single_select_is_none_of, link_row_has, link_row_has_not, link_row_contains, link_row_not_contains, boolean, empty, not_empty, multiple_select_has, multiple_select_has_not, multiple_collaborators_has, multiple_collaborators_has_not, user_is, user_is_not, has_value_equal, has_not_value_equal, has_value_contains, has_not_value_contains, has_value_contains_word, has_not_value_contains_word, has_value_length_is_lower_than, has_all_values_equal, has_empty_value, has_not_empty_value, has_any_select_option_equal, has_none_select_option_equal, has_value_lower, has_value_lower_or_equal, has_value_higher, has_value_higher_or_equal, has_not_value_higher_or_equal, has_not_value_higher, has_not_value_lower_or_equal, has_not_value_lower, has_date_equal, has_not_date_equal, has_date_before, has_not_date_before, has_date_on_or_before, has_not_date_on_or_before, has_date_on_or_after, has_not_date_on_or_after, has_date_after, has_not_date_after, has_date_within, has_not_date_within. **Please note that if this parameter is provided, all other `filter__{field}__{filter}` will be ignored, as well as the `filter_type` parameter.** |
| `order_by` | `string \| null` | No | Optionally the rows can be ordered by provided field ids separated by comma. By default a field is ordered in ascending (A-Z) order, but by prepending the field with a '-' it can be ordered descending (Z-A). |

### importDataAsync

`tables.importDataAsync`

Import data in the specified table if the authorized user has access to the related database's workspace. This endpoint is asynchronous and return the created job to track the progress of the task.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.tables.importDataAsync({
	table_id: 1001,
	data: [['example']],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `table_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Import data into the table related to the provided value. |
| `data` | `any[][]` | Yes | A list of rows you want to add to the specified table. Each row is a list of values, one for each **writable** field. The field values must be ordered according to the field order in the table, or according to `configuration.import_fields` when provided. All values must be compatible with the corresponding field type. Ex: ```json [ ["row1_field1_value", "row1_field2_value"], ["row2_field1_value", "row2_field2_value"], ] ``` for adding two rows to a table with two writable fields. |
| `configuration` | `object` | No | Additional table import configuration. |
| `importer_type` | `string` | No | The frontend importer identifier used to parse the file. |
| `original_file_name` | `string` | No | The original name of the uploaded file. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="configuration full type">

```ts
{
  import_fields?: number[] | null,
  upsert_fields?: number[] | null,
  upsert_values?: any[][] | null,
  skipped_fields?: number[] | null
}
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `type` | `any \| null` | No | The type of the job. |
| `progress_percentage` | `number \| null` | No | A percentage indicating how far along the job is. 100 means that it's finished. |
| `state` | `string \| null` | No | Indicates the state of the import job. |
| `human_readable_error` | `string \| null` | No | A human readable error message indicating what went wrong. |
| `error_code` | `string \| null` | No | A machine readable error code indicating why the job failed. |
| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `updated_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `database_id` | `number \| null` | No | Database id where the table will be created. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | The name of the new table. |
| `table_id` | `number \| null` | No | Table id where the data will be imported. |
| `first_row_header` | `boolean \| null` | No | — |
| `importer_type` | `string \| null` | No | The frontend importer identifier used to parse the file. |
| `original_file_name` | `string \| null` | No | The original name of the uploaded file. |
| `report` | `object \| null` | No | Import error report. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="report full type">

```ts
{
  failing_rows?: Record<string, Record<string, string[]>> | null
} | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

Lists all the tables that are in the database related to the database_id parameter if the user has access to the database's workspace. A table is exactly as the name suggests. It can hold multiple fields, each having their own type and multiple rows. They can be added via the….

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.tables.list({ database_id: 1 });
```

### order

`tables.order`

Changes the order of the provided table ids to the matching position that the id has in the list. If the authorized user does not belong to the workspace it will be ignored. The order of the not provided tables will be set to 0.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.tables.order({
	database_id: 1,
	table_ids: [1001],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `database_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | Updates the order of the tables in the database related to the provided value. |
| `table_ids` | `number[]` | Yes | Table ids in the desired order. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### createInvitation

`teams.createInvitation`

Invites an email address to the team. The person joins the workspace without a workspace role, so that the role of the team applies, and is added to the team once they accept. If a pending invitation already exists for the address, the team is added to it. The invitation email is sent out….

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.teams.createInvitation({ team_id: 1, email: 'ada@example.com' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `team_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The team the invitations add people to. |
| `email` | `string` | Yes | The email address of the person that is invited to the team. |
| `captcha_token` | `string` | No | The captcha token proving the request comes from a person, only required if a captcha provider is enabled for workspace invitations. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `invitation_id` | `number \| null` | No | The workspace invitation that adds the person to the team once accepted. |
| `email` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `team_id` | `number \| null` | No | The team the person joins once the invitation is accepted. |
| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |



---

### createInvitationLink

`teams.createInvitationLink`

Creates a permanent link that anyone can use to join the team. People who aren't a member of the workspace yet join it without a workspace role, so that the role of the team applies, and members of the workspace are added to the team. The link has no role of its own.

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.teams.createInvitationLink({ team_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `team_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The team the invitations add people to. |
| `name` | `string` | No | A name that reminds the admins what the link is for. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `workspace` | `number \| null` | No | The workspace that people join through the link. |
| `team_id` | `number \| null` | No | The team the link adds people to. |
| `name` | `any \| null` | No | A name that reminds the admins what the link is for. |
| `slug` | `string \| null` | No | The unique slug of the public link URL. |
| `has_password` | `boolean \| null` | No | Whether people must enter a password before they can use the link. |
| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

Changes the name of an invitation link to the team or its password.

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.teams.updateInvitationLink({ invitation_link_id: 1, team_id: 1 });
```

| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |

## Templates

### delete

`templates.delete`

Deletes a user template. Its owner can delete it in any state, and an instance admin can delete any user template. It's gone for everybody right away, and its revisions and content are removed later. The applications installed from it are kept. This can't be undone.

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.templates.delete({ slug: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | `string` | Yes | The slug of the template to delete. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Baserow accepted the call; it answered with no body. |



---

### download

`templates.download`

Responds with the URL of the archive of a user template, which imports like a workspace export. The archive is built on the first download: while there is none, a job that builds it is started instead, or the one of the user that builds it already is responded with. Once the job is finished, the….

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.templates.download({ slug: 'example', revision_id: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `templateAuthorization` | `string` | No | The token of the private link of a user template, which gives access to it while it's private. |
| `slug` | `string` | Yes | The slug of the user template to download. |
| `revision_id` | `number` | Yes | The id of the revision of the user template that the user was shown. Its owner and the instance admins may download any revision. Anyone else downloads the public revision, or the latest one of a template that isn't public with the token of its private link. |



**Output:** `object`

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Output full type">

```ts
{
  url?: string | null,
  file_name?: string | null
} | {
  id?: number | null,
  type?: any | null,
  progress_percentage?: number | null,
  state?: string | null,
  human_readable_error?: string | null,
  error_code?: string | null,
  created_on?: string | null,
  updated_on?: string | null,
  slug?: any | null | null,
  revision_id?: number | null | null,
  template_name?: any | null | null
}
```
</Accordion>

### installAsync

`templates.installAsync`

Start an async job to install the applications of the given template into the given workspace if the user has access to that workspace. The response contains those newly created applications. A user template can be installed by its owner, by the instance admins, by anyone signed in while it's….

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.templates.installAsync({ template_id: 1, workspace_id: 101 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `templateAuthorization` | `string` | No | The token of the private link of a user template, which gives access to it while it's private. |
| `clientSessionId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular client session. Then using the undo/redo endpoints with the same ClientSessionId header this action can be undone/redone. |
| `clientUndoRedoActionGroupId` | `string` | No | An optional header that marks the action performed by this request as having occurred in a particular action group.Then calling the undo/redo endpoint with the same ClientSessionId header, all the actions belonging to the same action group can be undone/redone together in a single API call. |
| `latest` | `boolean` | No | Installs the latest revision of a user template, also while it's public. Only its owner may ask for it. Ignored for official templates. |
| `revision_id` | `number \| string` | No | The `revision_id` of the user template that was shown. If another revision would be installed, because the template was updated since, nothing is installed. Ignored for official templates. |
| `template_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The id related to the template that must be installed. |
| `workspace_id` | `number \| string` | Yes | The id related to the workspace where the template applications must be installed into. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `type` | `any \| null` | No | The type of the job. |
| `progress_percentage` | `number \| null` | No | A percentage indicating how far along the job is. 100 means that it's finished. |
| `state` | `string \| null` | No | Indicates the state of the import job. |
| `human_readable_error` | `string \| null` | No | A human readable error message indicating what went wrong. |
| `error_code` | `string \| null` | No | A machine readable error code indicating why the job failed. |
| `created_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `updated_on` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `workspace` | `object \| null` | No | — |
| `template` | `object \| null` | No | — |
| `installed_applications` | `any \| null` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="workspace full type">

```ts
{
  id?: number | null,
  name?: string | null,
  generative_ai_models_enabled?: any | null
} | null
```

### list

`templates.list`

Lists the templates. The template's workspace_id can be used for previewing purposes because that workspace contains the applications that are in the template. All the get and list endpoints related to that workspace are accessible to whoever can list the template. The view query parameter….

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.templates.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `category` | `number` | No | Only templates in the category with this id. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `limit` | `number` | No | How many templates to return, at most 100. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `listed` | `boolean` | No | Only the templates everybody can open, each as everybody sees it: the official templates, unless `type=user`, and the public revision of the public user templates. The authenticated user's own come first, then the most recently listed. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `offset` | `number` | No | The offset of the templates to return. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `owned` | `boolean` | No | Only templates owned by the authenticated user. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `search` | `string` | No | Only templates whose name or description contains this value. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `type` | `official \| user` | No | Only templates of this type. Only with `view=flat`. |
| `view` | `flat \| public_categories` | No | `flat` responds with a paginated list of templates, `public_categories` with the categories of the public user templates, without the official ones. Otherwise, the response is the list of categories with their official templates, which is deprecated. |



**Output:** `object \| object[]`

### rotatePrivateLinkToken

`templates.rotatePrivateLinkToken`

Replaces the token of the private link of a user template owned by the user, which takes the access away from everybody who has the old link. The new token is in private_link_token. A template without a private link keeps having none. The private link of a blocked template can't be changed.

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.baserow.api.templates.rotatePrivateLinkToken({ slug: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | `string` | Yes | The slug of the template whose private link is regenerated. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `number \| null` | No | — |
| `revision_id` | `number \| null` | No | The id of the serialized revision. Sent with an install, so that the template isn't installed if it was updated since. |
| `type` | `string \| null` | No | Whether it's an official or a user template. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `slug` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `description` | `string \| null` | No | The description of this revision. |
| `icon` | `string \| null` | No | The icon class name that can be used for displaying purposes. |
| `keywords` | `any \| null` | No | — |
| `workspace_id` | `number \| null \| null` | No | The group containing the applications related to the template. The read endpoints related to that group are publicly accessible for preview purposes. Revisions of the same template that only differ in their details share it. |
| `is_default` | `any \| null` | No | Indicates if the template must be selected by default. The web-frontend automatically selects the first `is_default` template that it can find. |
| `open_application` | `number \| null \| null` | No | The application ID that must be opened when the template is previewed. If null, then the first will automatically be chosen. |
| `author_name` | `any \| null \| null` | No | The first name of the author of a user template. Null for an official template or a deleted author. |
| `is_own` | `boolean \| null` | No | Whether the authenticated user owns this user template. |
| `updated_on` | `string \| null` | No | When the content shown was last changed: the creation of the revision of a user template, the last update of an official one. |
| `categories` | `object[] \| null` | No | — |
| `state` | `string \| any \| null \| null \| null` | No | The state of the template as shown to its owner, and to instance admins on the template page. Null for anyone else. |
| `reason` | `any \| null` | No | Why the template was rejected or blocked, if given. Only shown to its owner, and to instance admins on the template page. |
| `can_make_public` | `boolean \| null \| null` | No | Whether making the template public lists it or sends it to review: it's not blocked, in review, or listed as it is. Only shown to its owner, null on listed rows. |
| `make_public_needs_review` | `boolean \| null \| null` | No | Whether making the template public sends it to the review of an instance admin, because approval is required or an admin rejected it since it was last approved. Only shown to its owner, null on listed rows. |
| `update_needs_review` | `boolean \| null \| null` | No | Whether an update of the template sends it to the review of an instance admin: when it's listed and approval is required or an admin rejected it since it was last approved, or when it's in review already. Only shown to its owner. |
| `listed` | `boolean \| null \| null` | No | Whether a revision of the template is listed for everybody, also while a later one is in review or rejected. Only shown to its owner, and to instance admins on the template page. |
| `source_workspace_id` | `number \| null` | No | The workspace the applications of the latest revision were copied from, if known. Only shown to its owner. |
